pr_body:
This makes sure that we only serve a hit from the request cache if it
was build using the same mapping and that the same mapping is used for
the entire "query phase" of the search.

Closes #62033
pr_title: Bust the request cache when the mapping changes (backport of #66295)

review_comment: this threw me off: how can typeExists be replaced with an equality check?

Weird, right? There is only one type in an index in 7.x and either the type you are searching is it or it ain't. There was some complexity around getting the `_default_` mapper, but you could only get it if the there isn't a type. Check out `MapperService#documentMapper(String type)` for the trick. I only changed this so we'd use the snapshot.
And, to top it off, there can't *not* be a type and be documents in the index. So all that funny stuff around `_default_` doesn't do anything in this case.

If there is a default mapping, this call `mapperService.documentMapper(type)` returns a non-null mapper for the `_default_` type. So this refactor may change the `type` query behavior slightly. This seems acceptable since default mappings were deprecated in 6.0 and the `type` query isn't completely clear on this behavior, but it felt worth pointing out.

I think it only returns something for `_default_` if there isn't another mapping. Which, I think, only happens when the index is in the process of being made. Though, I can fiddle with it a bit to see if a totally empty mapping gets it.
I played around a bit - I don't think you can have documents in the index and not have a `DocumentMapper`. So I *think* this is safe.
And if it isn't then that change is quite small.
